name: nav-clearance-vehicle-gap
description: #1154: NavGrid.NavCell.clearance gates a vehicle out of a 1-cell-wide gap an employee on foot can still use. Two management_office T1 buildings (2x2 footprint each) are placed at (20,20) and (23,20), leaving exactly one open column at x=22 between their east/west edges — a doorway wide enough for NAV_CLEARANCE_EMPLOYEE_CELLS (1) but narrower than NAV_CLEARANCE_VEHICLE_CELLS (2). An employee dispatched on foot from the west side (18,20) to the east side (25,20) crosses through that column. A second employee, dispatched the same way but mounted on a debris_hauler (`employee dispatch ... vehicle:debris_hauler`, which routes through Pathfinding.findPath with the vehicle's own requiredClearance via Vehicle.vehicleRequiredClearanceCells), must detour around one end of the building pair instead — the gap column itself is impassable to it. Every crossing is proven via `pendingActionCount` returning to 0 within a bounded `wait_until` (no per-entity x/z field exists in the state-dump schema to assert final position directly, so arrival is what `pendingActionCount` reaching 0 for a `general_work` dispatch already proves elsewhere in this suite, e.g. level-ground-then-build.json's identical pattern) — this file cannot yet assert the DETOUR itself, only that both crossings still complete; the exact route difference is what tests/unit/nav/Pathfinding.test.ts's own 'clearance-aware pathfinding (#1154)' suite proves against PathResult.waypoints directly, which this console-driven scenario has no equivalent field for. Before #1154 lands, requiredClearance is not gated at all, so both crossings simply take the short route and this file's own wait_until bounds all pass trivially; nothing here can fail red until the feature exists to narrow the gap.

steps.description: cash:200000 (default staffed cash is $50,000): two management_office orders cost $16,000 combined, and the roster's staffed payroll (PAY_CYCLE_TICKS) drains steadily across the ~250+ ticks the two construction orders and four dispatch crossings below cost in total — a run that goes bankrupt mid-scenario is a defect in the fixture, not a legitimate outcome for a scenario that isn't testing bankruptcy.
West wall of the doorway: management_office T1's 2x2 footprint covers (20,20)-(21,21). Real BuildMenu click flow — role: player, per level-ground-then-build.json's identical pattern.
East wall of the doorway: management_office T1's 2x2 footprint covers (23,20)-(24,21). Leaves exactly column x=22 (rows z=20-21) open between the two buildings — the 1-cell-wide gap.
Drain both queued construction orders — the staffed roster has no skill gate on place_building (requiredSkill: null), so whichever idle employee reaches each site first builds it.

Pre-position driller #1 on the west side of the doorway, on foot — `employee dispatch` has no UI equivalent (BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST), matching vehicle-traffic.json's `vehicle driver` bootstrap pattern.

Employee case: cross the doorway on foot from (18,20) to (25,20) — requiredClearance defaults to NAV_CLEARANCE_EMPLOYEE_CELLS (1) inside findPath, which the x=22 gap column satisfies, so the short straight route through it stays legal.

Proves the foot crossing completes — the general_work action drains from pendingActionCount only once employee #1 has both arrived and finished the token work at the target. No per-entity x/z field exists in the state-dump schema (GAME_STATE_SCHEMA) to assert the final (25,20) position directly; this is the same proof-of-arrival level-ground-then-build.json's own wait_until step relies on for a dispatched worker.

Pre-position driver #3 (driving.truck-qualified, per STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION) on the west side, mounted on the staffed debris_hauler — `vehicle:debris_hauler` on `employee dispatch` routes the itinerary through boarding it first, no separate `vehicle driver` bootstrap needed (confirmed live: the console accepts this in one command).

Vehicle case: cross from (18,21) to (25,21) mounted on the debris_hauler — requiredClearance is Vehicle.vehicleRequiredClearanceCells(vehicle) = NAV_CLEARANCE_VEHICLE_CELLS (2), which the x=22 gap column (clearance 1, one cell from each building wall) does not satisfy. Once #1154 gates isImpassable on clearance, this crossing can no longer use the gap and must detour around one end of the building pair instead.

Proves the mounted crossing still completes even though the direct gap is closed to it — a looser tick budget than the foot crossing's, since a real detour around the building pair is a longer route than the straight line through the doorway. Same proof-of-arrival limitation as the foot-crossing step above: no per-entity x/z field exists to assert (25,21) directly, or to assert the detour's shape — that belongs to tests/unit/nav/Pathfinding.test.ts's 'clearance-aware pathfinding (#1154)' suite, which reads PathResult.waypoints directly.
